results.evidence: Front view of a shirt collar with the collar-BAND front outlined in a faint red overlay, sitting under the crossed collar leaves and above the placket button. Isolating the red channel shows an asymmetric band end: a straight vertical edge on the left meeting the bottom edge in a hard ~90 degree corner (square), while the right side sweeps up in a curve rather than a corner (round). Correct garment part and the asymmetry is legible, though the red overlay is very weak (peak red-minus-neutral only 41/255) at 224x226.

Clean 192x192 front view of a shirt collar with the collar stand front highlighted in bright red. The red outline is a smooth continuous curve on both sides forming a rounded band end, with exactly ONE button centred in it. Plainly a round collar stand.

Same 192x192 template as the round stand, but the red-highlighted stand front has a straight vertical left edge meeting the bottom in a sharp square corner, and TWO red buttons stacked vertically inside it. Both the square profile and the 2-button count are unambiguous.

This file is BYTE-IDENTICAL to /images/collar_stand/square-collar-stand-with-2-buttons.jpg (md5 6455ac38074c68d4ebaed987b8b90bcd for both) and therefore shows TWO stacked buttons in the red-highlighted stand. It is being used for option cs-square 'Square Collar Stand' (catalog description: 'Square stand - structured and formal'), whose sibling cs-square-2btn is 'Square stand with two-button closure'. The button count is exactly what separates the two options, and this drawing depicts the 2-button variant - the filename itself reads 'square-collar-stand-with-2-buttons'. Side by side the two options would be pixel-for-pixel the same image.

180x180 flat/opened-out drawing of the collar and its band viewed from the underside (buttonhole at the left band end, button at the right band end). Isolating the red channel reveals a symmetric mirrored pair of narrow angled slivers, one in each collar leaf, angled toward the collar points - i.e. the two collar-stay slots. Correct garment part and correct feature location, but the discriminator against its siblings (stay-fixed 'Fixed (Permanent)', stay-none, stay-hidden-btn) is whether the pocket has an open mouth you can slide a stay out of, and at 180px with a near-invisible overlay that cannot be read.

3/4 view of a shirt collar worn OPEN - leaves splayed outward and lying flat like small revers, deep V neckline, no throat button, small loop-and-button at the left front, shaded undercollar band at the back. That reads plausibly as a camp/Cuban collar. However this is a SHARED template: shape-distance to point-in-85cm-with-button.jpg is 0.027 and to dr-point-in-58cm.jpg 0.031 and to standard-collar-with-75cm-collar-stand.jpg 0.031 (true duplicates in this folder score 0.003; genuinely distinct siblings score 0.05+). Four different SKUs use the same 'collar worn open' drawing with no dimension annotation, so it cannot uniquely express the Cuban discriminator (flat revere, no band, no throat closure - the catalog's own wording), and this drawing does show a stand and a throat loop.

Proper house-style tech pack: closed shirt collar, throat button on the stand, gently concave (curved) leaf edges, annotated '115.00' degrees in blue. Red/blue outline overlay against curved-in-9cm.jpg shows real divergence at the collar tips and the dimension rays, so it is a genuinely distinct drawing, and 115 vs 125 forms a coherent pair with the 9.0 cm option. The literal '8.0 cm' point length is not annotated, but the collar is visibly shorter-pointed than its 9.0 cm sibling.

Closed shirt collar with gently concave leaf edges and a throat button, annotated '125.00' degrees - one step wider and longer-pointed than curved-in-8cm.jpg ('115.00'). Coherent within the curved family. NOTE: french-in-75cm.jpg is the same drawing with the same '125.00' annotation (see that entry); the collision is charged to the French option, not this one, because curved 115/125 is an internally consistent progression and the house's real French drawing (french-in-8cm.jpg) is '145.00'.

Annotated '115.00' degrees. Zoomed in, each collar leaf plainly carries a SECOND shorter under-leaf with its own edge stitching sitting behind the outer leaf - the double-collar construction - plus a throat button on a tab below the leaf crossing and a small button on each leaf. Short points consistent with 5.5 cm. Double construction, cut-away spread and the button are all visible.

Not a point collar at all. It is the shared 'collar worn open' template - collar unbuttoned, leaves splayed flat, deep V, loop-and-button at the left front, no dimension annotation - and it registers almost exactly on cuban-collar.jpg (shape distance 0.031), standard-collar-with-75cm-collar-stand.jpg (0.025) and point-in-85cm-with-button.jpg (0.029). The house's actual 5.8 cm point collars in the same folder (fashion-point-in-58cm.jpg and point-in-58cm-with-button.jpg) are drawn CLOSED with short points and a blue '60.00' degree annotation. This drawing shows neither the 5.8 cm short point nor any dimension.

This is the Curved 9.0 cm drawing. It is annotated '125.00' degrees - the exact same value as curved-in-9cm.jpg - and a red/blue ink overlay of the two shows them registering line-for-line (same leaf shape, same tip position, same stand front, same throat button); only resampling fringe separates them. A French collar per the catalog is 'extremely wide-spread, with points that angle dramatically toward the shoulder seams', and the house does have that drawing: french-in-8cm.jpg is annotated '145.00' degrees with a visibly much wider spread. At 125 degrees this is a curved collar, and the customer would see the identical picture on both the French 7.5 cm and Curved 9.0 cm options.

Annotated '4.5cm', '3.5cm' and '90.00' degrees. Zoomed on the leaf ends, each leaf terminates in a flat horizontal cut rather than a taper to a point, so the leaf outline is faceted/multi-sided: the 4.5cm dimension runs along the angled front edge and the 3.5cm along the blunt bottom edge. That is exactly the hexagonal/chamfered leaf profile the label claims. Also the most distinctive drawing in the folder (nearest neighbour only 0.067).

Genuine house-style spread-collar tech pack, closed with a throat button, annotated '100.00' degrees, and distinct from every sibling (nearest neighbours middle-cut-away-in-85cm.jpg 0.067 and large-cut-away-in-8cm.jpg 0.068, versus 0.003 for a true duplicate). It sits in a distinct progression within its own family (large cut-away 7.5cm='115.00', 8.0cm='105.00', 8.2cm='100.00'). Caveat: the 8.2 cm point length itself is never written on the drawing.

Real shirt-collar tech pack, closed, throat button, long points, annotated '90.00' degrees. But it is a near-duplicate of regular-collar-19.jpg - shape distance 0.031, the third-closest pair in the entire folder - which is also annotated '90.00' and differs only by a small triangular patch at the left collar point. Both options are live in the catalog, so the 'cut-away' claim (an outward-angled spread, wider than a regular collar) is not expressed: it is drawn at the same 90 degrees as the Regular Collar 19. The 8.5 cm point length is not annotated either.

Shows a low rounded BAND/stand collar with no fold-over leaf and no collar points at all, closed at the centre front with a single button on the band. There is no tab. The house style does draw a real tab - regular-collar-in-85cm-with-tab.jpg in the same folder shows the collar leaves open with a horizontal fabric tab strip bridging them, bar-tacked, annotated '60.00' degrees. This drawing is instead nearly the same as rolled-stand-collar.jpg (shape distance 0.059) and one-piece-collar-in-75cm-with-tab.jpg (0.040). Neither the turndown one-piece leaf nor the tab is depicted.

An upright mandarin/band collar: front edges butt together at a plain vertical seam, no fold-over leaf, no collar points, no button on the band (only a small button-and-loop further down the placket), and no tab anywhere. Line art is also washed out and low-contrast (smallest file in the folder at 4192 bytes). Compare regular-collar-in-85cm-with-tab.jpg, which shows an actual throat tab. Neither 'One-Piece' turndown construction nor 'with Tab' is depicted.

Same failure as its 8.0 and 8.5 cm siblings: an upright band/stand collar with a narrow vertical underlap strip at the centre front, no fold-over leaf, no collar points, and no throat tab. Clusters with one-piece-collar-in-85cm-with-tab.jpg (0.065) and squared-stand-collar.jpg (0.095) rather than with any tab-collar drawing. The 'with Tab' feature named in the label is absent.

Closed shirt collar, throat button, moderate spread annotated '90.00' degrees, plus a small triangular reinforcement patch with an eyelet at the left collar point. Consistent with the catalog's 'moderately spread everyday collar (pattern #19)', and clearly distinguishable from Regular Collar 21 ('145.00'). Noted: it is a near-duplicate of middle-cut-away-in-85cm.jpg (0.031) apart from that triangular patch.

Closed shirt collar annotated '145.00' degrees with a rounded stand front carrying a button; visibly and hugely different from Regular Collar 19 ('90.00'), so the two live options are easy to tell apart. Pattern number '21' is not independently verifiable from the drawing. Noted: it is close to french-in-8cm.jpg (0.042) and to stand-collar-5cm.jpg (0.053), which are also '145.00' - a three-file collision, but only stand-collar-5cm.jpg is wrong on its own terms (see that entry).

Annotated '80.00' degrees. Short collar leaves whose ends are cut blunt/square rather than tapering to a sharp point, consistent with a 5.0 cm square collar; an octagonal throat button is drawn on the stand and, unlike the plain small-square-in-5cm.jpg, this version adds a small button/eyelet at each leaf end - which is the difference the 'with Button' label refers to.

The catalog defines this as 'A 5.0 cm upright band collar with NO fold-over leaf, circling the neck cleanly in the Mandarin or Nehru manner.' The drawing shows the opposite: a wide-spread TURNDOWN collar with two fold-over leaves crossing at the front, a rounded stand front with a button, annotated '145.00' degrees. It is also effectively the same drawing as french-in-8cm.jpg (0.052) and regular-collar-21.jpg (0.053), both '145.00'. The folder does contain genuine band-collar drawings (rolled-stand-collar.jpg, the one-piece-collar-in-*cm files) and they look nothing like this. Note this file is byte-identical to /images/techpacks/shirt/lapel/stand-collar-5cm.jpg (md5 256fa79278d5b76b214066fce69f53d2).
